quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #5
										  					
  

50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: You are driving on a narrow road and meet an oncoming vehicle. What must you do?

options.text: Pull completely off the road and stop.
Give the oncoming vehicle at least half of the road space.
Demand the other vehicle pull over.
Turn on your high beams so the other driver sees you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Give the oncoming vehicle at least half of the road space.
questions.explanation: On narrow roads, you must give oncoming vehicles at least half of the road space. Both drivers need enough space to pass safely.

questions.question: Your reaction time becomes slower after:

options.text: Drinking alcohol.
Sleeping.
Working hard.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drinking alcohol.
questions.explanation: Alcohol slows your reflexes and reaction time. It also reduces your vision and makes you less alert. The more alcohol you drink, the worse your judgment and driving skills become. You will have trouble judging distances, speeds, and where other vehicles are going.

questions.question: What type of sign is this?

options.text: Stop
Wrong way
Yield
Do not enter

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield
questions.explanation: This triangular sign is a "Yield" sign. Slow down and check for traffic. Give the right-of-way to pedestrians and other vehicles. Stop only if necessary.

questions.question: The center line has one solid yellow line and one broken yellow line. The broken yellow line is next to your lane. What does this mean?

options.text: You cannot pass other vehicles here.
You can pass other vehicles on the left if no traffic is coming the other way.
You can only make right turns in this area.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can pass other vehicles on the left if no traffic is coming the other way.
questions.explanation: When the broken yellow line is on your side, you can pass. The solid yellow line is on the other side, so oncoming traffic cannot pass.

questions.question: What should you do when you reach a traffic light that is not working?

options.text: Come to a full stop. Give the right-of-way before entering.
You don't need to stop if the intersection looks clear.
Drive quickly through to get out of the way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a full stop. Give the right-of-way before entering.
questions.explanation: When a traffic light is not working, treat the intersection like a four-way stop sign. Always come to a complete stop. Look both ways and yield to other traffic before entering.

questions.question: Highway markings:

options.text: Are usually not important.
Are only found in construction zones.
Give information to drivers.
Are usually red and blue.

questions.correctAnswerText: Give information to drivers.
questions.explanation: Highway markings help drivers stay in the correct position on the road. They show safe passing zones and warn about upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: Your car breaks down on the highway. What should you do?

options.text: Stop in the right lane.
Park with all four wheels off the road, if possible.
Stop where you are.

questions.correctAnswerText: Park with all four wheels off the road, if possible.
questions.explanation: When your vehicle breaks down, move it completely off the traveled road if you can.

questions.question: You see a flashing red traffic light ahead. What should you do?

options.text: Slow down and yield the right-of-way.
Slow down and drive carefully through.
Stop completely. Check for traffic, then go when safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely. Check for traffic, then go when safe.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means stop. Come to a complete stop like you would at a stop sign. Yield to all traffic and pedestrians, then go when it is safe.

questions.question: You are in the right lane and want to move to the left lane. What should you do?

options.text: Check your rearview mirror for traffic behind you.
Look over your left shoulder for traffic in your blind spot.
Check your side mirror and turn on your signal.
Do all of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do all of the above.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, check your mirrors and look over your shoulder to see your blind spot. Always signal before you change lanes.

questions.question: When entering the interstate, you find a gap in traffic, match the speed, and signal. What should you do next?

options.text: Expect other drivers to make room for you since you have the right-of-way.
Merge carefully into the gap.
Wait for the lane to completely clear before merging.

questions.correctAnswerText: Merge carefully into the gap.
questions.explanation: After finding a gap and matching traffic speed, merge carefully into it. Do not expect other drivers to move out of your way. Stay alert to all traffic around you.

questions.question: Driving slower than other traffic is:

options.text: A good idea in bad weather.
Okay if you don't know the speed limit.
Often dangerous because other drivers may get frustrated and try to pass you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Often dangerous because other drivers may get frustrated and try to pass you.
questions.explanation: Driving slower than other traffic can be dangerous. Drivers behind you may get impatient and take dangerous risks to pass you.

questions.question: This sign is a:

options.text: Yield sign.
School crossing sign.
Stop sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield sign.
questions.explanation: A downward-facing triangle always means yield. You must slow down or stop when you see a yield sign.

questions.question: What should you worry most about when you see this sign?

options.text: Your headlights being out of alignment because one side of your car is higher.
Damaging a tire if you drift onto the shoulder.
Hydroplaning if water is on the shoulder.
Losing control of your vehicle if you drift onto the shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Losing control of your vehicle if you drift onto the shoulder.
questions.explanation: This sign means the shoulder is lower than the road ahead. If one wheel drops onto the low shoulder, do not slam on the brakes or steer sharply. This can cause you to lose control of your vehicle.

questions.question: You may drive around or under a railroad crossing gate that is being lowered or raised:

options.text: As long as the train is not too close.
If your vehicle won't damage the gate.
If you look both ways first.
Never.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never.
questions.explanation: Flashing red lights, lowered gates, and bells at a railroad crossing mean you must stop completely. Do not cross the tracks until the lights and bells stop and the gates are fully up. Never drive around or under a moving gate.

questions.question: You should signal continuously while turning because it:

options.text: Is against the law to turn off your signal before finishing a turn.
Tells other drivers what you plan to do.
Is always unsafe to turn off a signal before finishing a turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tells other drivers what you plan to do.
questions.explanation: Always signal when turning, changing lanes, slowing down, or stopping. This tells other drivers, motorcyclists, bicyclists, and pedestrians what you plan to do.

questions.question: You may drive around railroad crossing gates:

options.text: When the train has passed.
Never.
When the lights stop flashing.
When other drivers drive around the gates.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never.
questions.explanation: Stop at all railroad crossings when warning signals appear. These signals include flashing red lights, lowered gates, a flagger, or the train's horn. Never try to go around a lowered gate.

questions.question: When passing a large vehicle, drivers of small vehicles should be ready for:

options.text: Loud noises.
Extra air pollution.
Strong wind gusts from the large vehicle.
Falling parts.

questions.correctAnswerText: Strong wind gusts from the large vehicle.
questions.explanation: Large vehicles create strong wind gusts that can push smaller vehicles. Drivers of small vehicles should be ready to steer correctly when approaching or passing large vehicles moving at high speeds.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Slow down and get ready to stop if cars are coming.
Stop completely, then go when it is safe.
Go carefully through the intersection without always stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely, then go when it is safe.
questions.explanation: An octagonal sign always means stop. Come to a complete stop at the stop line and go only when it is safe. If there is no stop line, stop before the crosswalk. If there is no crosswalk, stop before the intersection so you can see oncoming traffic.

questions.question: When getting ready to turn left, drivers should:

options.text: Slow down gradually while checking the rearview mirror.
Move into the left lane.
Watch for oncoming vehicles and pedestrians.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Before turning left, signal 3 to 5 seconds ahead. Check your rearview mirror and slow down gradually. On a road with multiple lanes, move into the left lane before the intersection. Give the right-of-way to traffic and pedestrians. Turn only when the path is clear.

questions.question: At an intersection with a yield sign, you:

options.text: Must let cross traffic go if it is close enough to cause a problem.
Must only yield to vehicles on your right.
Should slow down but never stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Must let cross traffic go if it is close enough to cause a problem.
questions.explanation: At a yield sign, let traffic in the lanes you want to enter go first. Be ready to stop if needed, but you can go without stopping if there are no other vehicles coming.

questions.question: You see a flashing red light at an intersection. What should you do?

options.text: Stop completely, then go when it is safe.
Stop only if other cars are coming.
Stop only if cars are already in the intersection.
Slow down and be ready to stop if needed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely, then go when it is safe.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means the same thing as a stop sign. You must stop, let others go first, then go when it is safe.

questions.question: What does a flashing yellow light at an intersection mean?

options.text: Slow down and go carefully.
Stop as fast as you can.
Stop and go only when the intersection is empty.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and go carefully.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means slow down and go carefully. You do not need to stop.

questions.question: You want to turn right at a corner. A person with a guide dog is waiting to cross in front of you. What should you do?

options.text: Turn off your engine until they cross.
Tell them when to cross.
Wait until they cross.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait until they cross.
questions.explanation: People using guide dogs or white canes must always be allowed to cross first.

questions.question: Two cars arrive at a four-way stop at the same time. What happens?

options.text: The car on the left must let the car on the right go first.
The car on the right must let the car on the left go first.
Drivers must use hand signals to communicate.
One driver should go without stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: The car on the left must let the car on the right go first.
questions.explanation: When two cars reach a four-way stop at the same time, the car on the left must yield to the car on the right.

questions.question: When can you go through a yellow light?

options.text: When an emergency vehicle is crossing your lane.
When people are crossing.
When you are turning right.
When you are already in the intersection when it turns yellow.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you are already in the intersection when it turns yellow.
questions.explanation: If the light turns yellow while you are in the intersection, you can continue carefully through it.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Two-way traffic.
Lane shifting.
Low clearance.
Added lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Two-way traffic.
questions.explanation: This yellow warning sign tells you that traffic is coming from the opposite direction.

questions.question: When passing a car on a two-lane road, what should you do?

options.text: Return to your lane when there is enough space between you and the car you passed.
Stay in the left lane if you plan to turn left.
Go back to the right side right away.
You can drive in either lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Return to your lane when there is enough space between you and the car you passed.
questions.explanation: After passing on a two-lane road, return to the right lane when you have enough space between you and the car you passed.

questions.question: How often should you check your rearview mirrors?

options.text: Often to see cars behind you.
To see if a car is in your blind spot.
Only when you are slowing down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Often to see cars behind you.
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors often so you always know where cars are around you.

questions.question: Which statement about large trucks is true?

options.text: They need more distance to stop than cars.
They all have air brakes that stop them quickly.
They can turn easier than cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: They need more distance to stop than cars.
questions.explanation: Large trucks need much longer to stop than cars. A car at 55 mph stops in about 400 feet. A large truck at 55 mph needs about 800 feet to stop.

questions.question: When changing lanes, what should you never do?

options.text: Change lanes inside an intersection.
Look over your shoulder to check your blind spot.
Watch for other cars moving into your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes inside an intersection.
questions.explanation: Never change lanes in an intersection. Always look over your shoulder to check your blind spot before changing lanes. Watch for other cars moving into the same lane.

questions.question: When is it most dangerous to turn or stop in rainy weather?

options.text: After it has been raining all day.
One half hour after it stops raining.
During the first half hour of rain.

questions.correctAnswerText: During the first half hour of rain.
questions.explanation: Be extra careful when turning and stopping during the first half hour of rain. Oil from cars mixes with rain water and makes the road very slippery.

questions.question: What should you do when driving on snow or ice?

options.text: It is safe to use your cruise control.
Make speed and directional changes more gradually than you would otherwise.
Drive as you would under normal conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make speed and directional changes more gradually than you would otherwise.
questions.explanation: On snow or ice, change your speed and direction slowly. Do not use cruise control on snow or ice because your tires can lose grip and you can lose control of your vehicle.

questions.question: When should your wheels NOT point straight ahead?

options.text: When waiting to make a left turn at a traffic light.
When parked on a hill or sloping driveway.
When parked on the side of a level roadway where there is no curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: When parked on a hill or sloping driveway.
questions.explanation: When parked on a hill, turn your wheels toward the curb. This prevents your vehicle from rolling into traffic if the brakes fail. When waiting to turn left at a light, keep wheels straight ahead. This protects you if another car hits you from behind.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: T intersection.
Lane shifting.
Side road.
Do not block intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: T intersection.
questions.explanation: This yellow warning sign alerts drivers to a T intersection ahead. Get ready to turn left or right.

questions.question: When can you drive on the shoulder to pass another car?

options.text: If the vehicle ahead of you is turning left.
Under no circumstances.
If the shoulder is wide enough.

questions.correctAnswerText: Under no circumstances.
questions.explanation: Never pass another vehicle on the shoulder. The other driver will not expect you there and may pull onto the shoulder, hitting you.

questions.question: What must you do when an emergency vehicle uses its siren and/or flashing lights?

options.text: Pull to the right and stop.
Pull to the right and slow down.
Pull to the right and turn on their vehicle's four-way flashers.
Stop and let the emergency vehicle pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull to the right and stop.
questions.explanation: When you see or hear an emergency vehicle with lights, sirens, or warning devices, immediately drive to the right side of the road and stop.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Traffic signal ahead.
Stop.
Yield the right-of-way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic signal ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a traffic signal is coming up.

questions.question: Which statement about driving speed is true?

options.text: As your speed increases, the chance of a fatality increases.
As your speed increases, so should your following distance.
Both of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above.
questions.explanation: Higher speeds increase the risk of death in a crash. At speeds above 80 miles per hour, your chance of surviving is almost zero. Higher speeds also mean longer stopping distances, so increase your following distance as you go faster.

questions.question: When can you turn right on a red light if no sign prohibits it?

options.text: Stop and turn from the lane farthest to the right.
Yield to pedestrians before turning.
Use your turn signal.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: To turn right on red, you must come to a complete stop, use your turn signal, yield to all cars and pedestrians, and turn from the rightmost lane.

questions.question: What should you do if you are driving in another driver's blind spot?

options.text: Move forward or drop back so the other driver can see you.
Keep a steady pace.
Stay in the driver's blind spot.
Honk to let them know you are there.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move forward or drop back so the other driver can see you.
questions.explanation: Do not stay in another driver's blind spot. Move forward or back so the other driver can see you.

questions.question: When driving on major highways, what should you do?

options.text: Stay alert.
Keep your eyes moving.
Be ready to react to road hazards.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: On highways, you must stay alert and be ready to react to unexpected hazards. Keep your eyes moving to avoid highway hypnosis. Do not look at one thing for more than a few seconds.

questions.question: When making a right turn on a green light, what must you do?

options.text: Maintain your normal driving speed.
Stop and look for nearby police cars.
Yield to pedestrians.
Increase your normal driving speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield to pedestrians.
questions.explanation: You may turn right on a green light unless a sign says otherwise. When turning, you must yield to other vehicles and pedestrians in the intersection.

questions.question: Having a driver license is a:

options.text: Requirement.
Privilege.
Right.

questions.correctAnswerText: Privilege.
questions.explanation: Driving is a privilege, not a right. All drivers must help keep everyone safe on the road. If you misuse this privilege, it can be taken away.

questions.question: If a tire suddenly goes flat while you are driving, what should you do?

options.text: Rapidly pump the brake pedal several times.
Slow down gradually and do not brake.
Press down on the brake pedal as hard as you can.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down gradually and do not brake.
questions.explanation: If a tire goes flat, grip the steering wheel firmly and keep the vehicle straight. Take your foot off the accelerator and do not brake. Let the vehicle slow on its own. Use the brakes gently only if needed. Pull off the road when it is safe.

questions.question: The driver ahead of you stops at a crosswalk. What should you do?

options.text: Cautiously pass the vehicle at 10 mph or slower.
Stop and proceed only when all pedestrians have crossed.
Change lanes, look carefully, and pass the stopped vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and proceed only when all pedestrians have crossed.
questions.explanation: Do not pass a vehicle stopped at a crosswalk. There may be pedestrians you cannot see. Instead, stop and move forward only after all pedestrians have crossed.

questions.question: If traffic signals at an intersection are not working due to a power outage, what should you do?

options.text: Park your vehicle as far off the road as possible and wait for power to be restored.
Use hand signals to indicate your intentions to other drivers.
Turn on your hazard lights and proceed through the intersection without stopping.
Treat the intersection as a four-way stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Treat the intersection as a four-way stop.
questions.explanation: When a traffic light is not working, treat the intersection like a four-way stop. Yield to other drivers just as you would at a four-way stop. Proceed through the intersection with caution when it is your turn.

questions.question: You need to use extra caution when driving near a pedestrian with a white cane because:

options.text: He or she is deaf.
He or she is a police officer.
He or she is blind.
He or she has poor balance.

questions.correctAnswerText: He or she is blind.
questions.explanation: A white cane or guide dog means the pedestrian is blind. Slow down, yield the right-of-way, and be prepared to stop. This helps prevent injury to the pedestrian.

questions.question: When you are being tailgated, what should you do?

options.text: Move over to the right if there is an open lane.
If no right lane is available, slow down gradually when the road ahead is clear to let the tailgater pass you.
Never slow down abruptly.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: If being tailgated, move to the right lane if one is open. If not, wait until the road ahead is clear, then slow down gradually to let the tailgater pass. Never brake suddenly, as this increases the risk of a rear-end collision.

questions.question: If you need to drive in foggy weather, what should you do?

options.text: Turn on your low beam headlights.
Turn on your hazard lights.
It is okay to drive at the maximum speed limit.
Do not drive at a speed above 10 miles per hour.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on your low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: Use your headlights when visibility is 500 feet or less. Use low beams in fog or rain. High beams reflect light back into your eyes and make it harder to see.

questions.question: What is the proper way to make a right turn?

options.text: Signal, slow down, and move into the lane closest to the centerline before turning.
Signal, slow down, and move into the lane closest to the right curb before turning.
Approach the corner in the right lane, but move toward the middle of the street before turning.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal, slow down, and move into the lane closest to the right curb before turning.
questions.explanation: Signal to warn other drivers of your turn. Slow down and approach from the right lane, staying as close to the right curb as possible.
